title: 2007 AMC 12A Problem 25
statement: Call a set of integers spacy if it contains no more than one out of any three consecutive integers. How many subsets of \(\{1,2,3,\ldots,12\},\) including the empty set, are spacy?

solutions.text:
Let \(c_n\) be the number of spacy subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}.\) A spacy subset either omits \(n\) (there are \(c_{n-1}\) of these) or contains \(n,\) in which case it omits \(n-1\) and \(n-2\) (there are \(c_{n-3}\) of these).

Hence \(c_n=c_{n-1}+c_{n-3},\) with \(c_1=2,\) \(c_2=3,\) \(c_3=4.\)

The sequence continues \(6,9,13,19,28,41,60,88,129,\) so \(c_{12}=129.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(c_n\) count the spacy subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\); condition on whether \(n\) is included
Excluding \(n\) gives \(c_{n-1}\); including it forbids \(n-1,n-2,\) giving \(c_{n-3},\) so \(c_n=c_{n-1}+c_{n-3}\)
